newsitem.title: Turkmenistan: Turkmens gather 456,000 T grain, 38 pct of target.
newsitem.headline: Turkmens gather 456,000 T grain, 38 pct of target.

text.p: Turkmenistan gathered 456,167 tonnes of grain as of June 23, or 38.1 percent of its total net grain target this year, an official from the State Statistics Committee said on Tuesday.
Turkmen President Saparmurat Niyazov, who enjoys a Soviet-era personality cult, has set a production target this year of 1.2 million tonnes of grain, rising to 2.0 million by 2000.
But Niyazov's plans to achieve grain self-sufficiency for his impoverished nation of around four million were dashed by last year's paltry harvest of 480,000 tonnes.
Turkmenistan started harvesting grain in early June, and Niyazov's press service said earlier that the campaign would be over by the end of this month.

The Agriculture Ministry has said the area sown to wheat this year had been reduced to 400,000 hectares from last year's 600,000 hectares, but added that it expected yields to rise to 3.0 tonnes per hectare from last year's meagre 0.8 tonnes.
Last year, when Turkmenistan faced severe bread shortages and had to import grain, Niyazov fired the agriculture minister and heads of the two main grain-growing regions.
